system:
You are an impartial methodological referee for a biomedical data-analysis agent. Two candidate analysis plans for the same scientific question have each been run at small scale. For each plan you receive its design and an evidence card: numbered facts measured in that pilot run and facts about how the plan validated itself. Decide which plan, if run in full, is more likely to give a valid answer to the question, with a conclusion that matches its evidence.

How to judge
1. Judge only from the objective and the evidence cards. Every reason you give must cite evidence ids; an argument without an id does not count.
2. Complexity is not a reason. That a method sounds advanced, modern or powerful counts for nothing; what it demonstrably did in the pilot counts.
3. A higher self-reported score is not sufficient. Each score was produced under that plan's own validation design. Read the validation-design items and ask what the score would mean under a strict design: Was the scoring target smoothed or cleaner than the real one? Was a configuration picked on the very folds that are reported? How many configurations did each comparison arm get? Is there any measure of spread, and is the difference between the plans larger than it?
4. Convergence. A model that had not converged has not shown what it can do, and its score is unreliable in both directions. Prefer evidence from converged training; do not reward an unconverged model for a promising number.
5. The comparison with the rulers and the simple reference on the same data matters more than the absolute score.
6. Fitness for the question. Prefer the plan whose design can actually deliver what the objective asks for (the estimand, the required comparators, the permitted conclusion).
7. Cost is a tie-breaker, and a disqualifier only when a full run would not fit the stated budget.
8. Declare a tie only when the evidence does not separate the plans.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"winner": "first" | "second" | "tie",
 "cited_evidence": [evidence ids you relied on],
 "reason": "at most 120 words, citing ids inline",
 "validity_concerns": {"first": [short strings], "second": [short strings]}}
prompt:
SCIENTIFIC QUESTION:
Using the paired RNA and ATAC measurements, learn the cross-modal relationship. For cells of the same donor that took no part in training and for which only ATAC is provided, for which genes can the variation in RNA expression be predicted reliably?

COMPILED OBJECTIVE:
{
 "task_family": "cross_modal_prediction",
 "analysis_unit": "single cell (individual nucleus from the single healthy PBMC donor)",
 "estimand": "Per-gene Pearson correlation between ATAC-predicted and binomial-thinned log-normalised RNA across unseen donor cells, and per-gene correlation gain over the ATAC cluster-mean baseline.",
 "target": "Log-normalised RNA expression of frozen in-scope genes per unseen cell, scored against an independent binomial-thinned half of raw UMI counts.",
 "allowed_inputs": [
  "Paired RNA UMI counts and ATAC peak fragment counts of development cells",
  "ATAC peak fragment counts of held-out cells at prediction time only",
  "Peak-to-gene annotations with TSS distances and promoter/distal flags, plus gene start coordinates",
  "Frozen list of in-scope genes and frozen baseline cluster count from development cells",
  "Curated joint-modality development cell-type annotations solely for descriptive summaries and within-cluster diagnostics on development splits"
 ],
 "forbidden_inputs": [
  "Held-out cells' RNA counts (full or thinned halves) during training, tuning, or prediction",
  "Held-out cells' ATAC counts during model training, preprocessing, latent-space fitting, clustering, or hyperparameter selection",
  "Curated WNN cell-type annotations as model inputs for unseen cells or as evaluation ground truth",
  "Smoothed, imputed, denoised, or unthinned full-depth RNA expression as the validation scoring target",
  "Validation-split cells' RNA or ATAC during training, feature transformation, baseline clustering, or model selection",
  "External donor datasets, atlases, or pretrained model weights outside the provided paired Multiome measurements"
 ],
 "required_comparators": [
  "Floor 1 (cell-type baseline): ATAC-cluster mean RNA expression using the frozen development cluster count",
  "Floor 2 (gene activity): unlearned sum of ATAC counts over promoter and linked nearby peaks",
  "Floor 3 (sequencing depth): regression predicting log-normalised RNA from log ATAC sequencing depth alone",
  "Floor 4 (simple learners): ridge, k-nearest-neighbour, and partial-least-squares regression on the ATAC latent space",
  "Noise ceiling: RNA-to-RNA model fit on training cells predicting unseen cells' thinned half B from half A",
  "Permutation null: cell-permuted correlation distribution used to identify unjudgeable genes whose ceiling fails noise"
 ],
 "primary_metric": "Per-gene Pearson correlation r against binomial-thinned log-normalised RNA (half B) across unseen cells, evaluated via paired-bootstrap correlation gain over the ATAC cluster-mean baseline and mean per-gene r.",
 "acceptance_criteria": [
  {
   "id": "A1",
   "statement": "Training, selection, and prediction use no held-out RNA, no held-out ATAC in fitting, and no WNN labels.",
   "check": "no_forbidden_inputs",
   "rule": "Verify input lineage so every learned transformation, cluster, and weight uses only allowed development-cell inputs."
  },
  {
   "id": "A2",
   "statement": "Preprocessing, ATAC latent embeddings, baseline clustering, and model selection are strictly nested without evaluation cells.",
   "check": "selection_nested",
   "rule": "Fit scalers, embeddings, clusters, and hyperparameter choices inside inner training folds; compute reported scores on untouched outer-fold cells."
  },
  {
   "id": "A3",
   "statement": "Validation correlations are computed against unsmoothed, binomial-thinned half-count log-normalised RNA of unseen cells.",
   "check": "scored_on_unsmoothed_truth",
   "rule": "Split each unseen validation cell's raw UMI counts via independent binomial thinning into halves A and B; score against log-normalised half B."
  },
  {
   "id": "A4",
   "statement": "Candidate model, noise ceiling, permutation null, and all floor baselines are scored on identical unseen cells.",
   "check": "both_arms_same_units",
   "rule": "Compute Pearson r across the exact same outer-fold cells, identical thinned target half B, frozen in-scope genes, and identical zero-variance handling."
  },
  {
   "id": "A5",
   "statement": "Biological claims require beating technical depth and gene-activity floors; reliable-gene claims require beating the cell-type floor.",
   "check": "beats_required_floors",
   "rule": "Derive floor thresholds from comparator scores on identical validation cells: aggregate mean r must exceed depth and gene-activity floors; adopted learners must justify complexity against simple learners."
  },
  {
   "id": "A6",
   "statement": "Gene-level claims of reliable prediction beyond cell identity control false discoveries across all in-scope genes.",
   "check": "multiplicity_controlled",
   "rule": "Place genes whose ceiling fails the permutation null into unjudgeable; call remaining genes reliable only if paired-bootstrap r exceeds Floor 1 after Benjamini-Hochberg across all in-scope genes at 5% FDR."
  },
  {
   "id": "A7",
   "statement": "Each in-scope gene's correlation estimate and gain over the cell-type baseline include 95% confidence intervals.",
   "check": "interval_reported",
   "rule": "Compute two-sided 95% confidence intervals empirically from the paired-bootstrap distribution across unseen evaluation cells."
  },
  {
   "id": "A8",
   "statement": "Deliverable includes the finite held-out prediction matrix, reliable gene list, and per-gene correlation intervals.",
   "check": "deliverable_complete",
   "rule": "Confirm matrix shape equals held-out cells by frozen in-scope genes on the log-normalised scale with only finite values, plus complete gene lists and intervals."
  }
 ],
 "conclusion_options": [
  "Unjudgeable due to measurement noise: for every in-scope gene, the RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling fails to exceed the cell-permutation null.",
  "Confounded by sequencing depth: judgeable genes exist, but ATAC predictors fail to exceed the technical ATAC-depth baseline across unseen donor cells.",
  "No gene predicted beyond cell identity: predictors beat the depth baseline, but no judgeable in-scope gene significantly beats the ATAC cluster-mean baseline at 5% FDR.",
  "Specific genes predicted beyond cell identity: predictors beat technical floors, and an identified non-empty set of judgeable genes beats the ATAC cluster-mean baseline at 5% FDR."
 ],
 "conclusion_scope": "Applies solely to unseen granulocyte-depleted PBMCs from this single healthy donor under the same Multiome assay; shows nothing about generalisation across other donors, tissues, disease states, granulocytes, or causal gene regulation."
}

MEASURED DIFFICULTIES OF THE DATA:
- D1 [measurement_noise, high] RNA counts are 85.3% zeros (median 3800 UMIs per cell). Splitting each cell's reads into two independent halves, a gene's value in one half correlates with the other half at a median r of 0.111 across 11282 in-scope genes (90th percentile 0.306).
- D2 [class_imbalance, high] The provided annotation has 19 cell types in the development set, from 1936 cells (CD14 Mono) down to 15 (Plasma).
- D3 [multiple_comparisons, high] 11282 genes are in scope and each gets its own test.
- D4 [label_provenance, high] The cell-type annotation supplied with the development cells was produced by clustering both modalities jointly (weighted nearest neighbours) and curating the clusters by hand. It is not an independent measurement.
- D5 [technical_confounding, medium] ATAC depth and RNA depth are correlated across cells (r = 0.36 on the log scale). A model that sees only ATAC depth reaches a mean per-gene r of 0.032.
- D6 [strong_baseline, medium] Predicting each cell by the mean expression of its ATAC cluster (k = 20, chosen by cross-validation inside the development set) gives a mean per-gene r of 0.130; ridge regression on the ATAC latent space gives 0.143; the RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling is 0.194.
- D7 [statistical_power, low] With thousands of cells a correlation as small as 0.037 already exceeds 95% of the permutation null (3124 held-out cells will be scored).

TASK CONSTRAINTS:
{
 "decision_rule": "\"Reliably predicted\" means predicted beyond cell identity. Each in-scope gene is placed in one of three groups: (0) cannot be judged - the ceiling itself is not above the permutation null for this gene; (1) not beyond the cell-type baseline - the method's r is not significantly above the cluster-mean baseline's r; (2) predicts variation beyond cell type - the method's r is significantly above the cluster-mean baseline's r (paired bootstrap over cells, Benjamini-Hochberg across all in-scope genes, false discovery rate 5%). Thresholds come from the data by these rules; only the 5% false discovery rate and the 95% confidence level are conventions. An answer of \"few or no genes are predicted beyond cell type\" is acceptable if that is what the evidence shows.",
 "how_predictions_are_scored": "The evaluator holds the RNA of the held-out cells. Each held-out cell's RNA reads were split at random into two independent halves, A and B (binomial thinning). Every method is scored against half B after log-normalisation: for each gene, the Pearson correlation r between predicted and observed values across held-out cells. Genes in scope and the cluster number of the cell-type baseline were frozen from development cells only and are part of the view.",
 "scope_of_inference": "cells of the same donor that were not used for training; nothing about other donors",
 "limits": {
  "n_plans": 6,
  "min_ambitious": 4,
  "n_candidates_requested": 8,
  "plans_per_call": 1,
  "full_run_minutes": 120,
  "cpus_per_job": 32
 }
}

=== FIRST PLAN (id P1) ===
DESIGN:
{
 "name": "Nested LSI Multi-Output Ridge Reference",
 "complexity": "simple_reference",
 "analysis_unit": "single cell",
 "inputs": {
  "lsi": {
   "n_components": 50,
   "max_peaks": 108377
  }
 },
 "preprocessing": [
  "Binarise ATAC peak fragment counts, fit TF-IDF inverse-document-frequency weights across all 108,377 peaks, and fit 51-component truncated SVD strictly on outer/inner training-fold development cells; drop component 1 (sequencing-depth axis) to retain 50 L2-normalised LSI features, projecting unseen validation and held-out cells out-of-sample without refitting.",
  "Normalise training-fold raw RNA UMI counts per cell via log1p(1e4 * UMI / total_cell_UMI) using total UMI summed across all 13,536 measured genes, then slice target columns to the frozen 11,282 in-scope genes.",
  "For unseen validation cells only, split raw RNA UMI counts via independent Binomial(UMI, 0.5) thinning into half A (solely for the RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling input) and half B, computing unsmoothed log1p(1e4 * half_B / total_half_B_UMI) on the frozen 11,282 genes as the evaluation target.",
  "Exclude held-out cells' ATAC and curated WNN labels from all fitting, clustering, and tuning steps, verify comparator sanity on synthetic known-answer checks, and set Pearson r = 0.0 identically across all arms whenever predicted or observed variance is zero."
 ],
 "model": {
  "component": "latent_ridge",
  "params": {
   "alpha": 100.0
  }
 },
 "training": {
  "target_denoising": "none",
  "inner_cv_folds": 4,
  "alpha_grid": [
   1.0,
   10.0,
   50.0,
   100.0,
   500.0,
   1000.0,
   5000.0
  ],
  "record_tuning_curve": true,
  "final_refit_scope": "all_7288_development_cells_only"
 },
 "validation": {
  "scheme": "kfold",
  "k": 5,
  "split_unit": "cell",
  "scoring_target": "thinned_half",
  "n_seeds": 3,
  "compare_with": [
   "floor_1_cell_type",
   "floor_2_gene_activity",
   "floor_3_depth",
   "floor_4_simple_learners",
   "ceiling",
   "permutation_null"
  ],
  "comparator_details": "Fit k='frozen' (k=20) cluster_mean, promoter_and_distal gene_activity_score, log-ATAC-depth OLS, latent_knn, latent_pls, and RNA-to-RNA ridge ceiling (half A to half B) strictly inside each outer training fold; evaluate all arms on identical out-of-fold cells and identical thinned half B targets.",
  "bootstrap_resamples": 1000,
  "gene_claim_rule": "Assign in-scope genes whose RNA-to-RNA ceiling fails to beat the 1,000-shuffle cell-permutation null (one-sided p >= 0.05) to group 0 (unjudgeable); for remaining judgeable genes, compute 1,000 paired cell-bootstrap resamples of delta_r = r_model - r_floor1, apply Benjamini-Hochberg across all 11,282 in-scope genes at 5% FDR, and call genes with BH q < 0.05 and delta_r > 0 group 2 (reliably predicted beyond cell type), otherwise group 1 (not beyond cell type), auditing seed-to-seed stability."
 },
 "metrics": [
  "Per-gene and mean Pearson correlation r against unsmoothed binomial-thinned log-normalised RNA (half B) across unseen out-of-fold cells",
  "Per-gene paired-bootstrap correlation gain (delta_r = r_model - r_floor1) and empirical two-sided 95% confidence intervals for both r_model and delta_r",
  "Gene counts and identities partitioned into (0) unjudgeable, (1) not-beyond-cell-type, and (2) reliably-predicted-beyond-cell-type at 5% BH-FDR across 11,282 genes",
  "Ratio of achieved correlation to the RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling (r_model / r_ceiling) across judgeable in-scope genes",
  "Within-cluster per-gene Pearson r across frozen ATAC clusters and descriptive development WNN cell types (including rare Plasma cells) alongside pooled r",
  "Empirical 95% CI coverage/width across folds, 3-seed selection spread, and automated A1-A8 verification of finite 3,124 x 11,282 held-out predictions"
 ],
 "allowed_conclusions": "Select strictly one of the four objective-defined conclusions supported by nested validation (unjudgeable due to noise, confounded by depth, no gene beyond cell identity, or a specific 5%-FDR gene set predicted beyond cell identity by linear global chromatin state), scoped exclusively to unseen granulocyte-depleted PBMCs of this single healthy donor under the same Multiome assay with no cross-donor, granulocyte, causal, or non-linear optimality claims.",
 "budget": {
  "needs_gpu": false,
  "pilot_minutes": 2.0,
  "full_minutes": 12.0,
  "cpus": 32
 }
}

SUMMARY:
Each cell's ATAC profile is projected into a depth-filtered Latent Semantic Indexing space fitted strictly on training cells, and ridge regression predicts expression across all 11,282 target genes. Using nested five-fold cross-validation over three seeds, predictions on unseen cells are scored against binomial-thinned RNA alongside technical floors, the ATAC cluster-mean baseline, and an RNA noise ceiling. Paired bootstraps with false-discovery control identify which judgeable genes exceed cell identity. This simple reference quantifies what global linear chromatin state achieves alone.

EVIDENCE CARD (pilot run):
[P1-E1] (self_score) Self-reported score: mean per-gene Pearson r = 0.1370 (SD 0.0038 over 2 splits), on 1500 genes; 1200 distinct validation cells enter the gene-level tests.
[P1-E2] (ruler) Required comparators on the same training and validation cells, genes and scoring target: noise ceiling (RNA-to-RNA) 0.1728; cluster-mean baseline 0.1223, ridge 0.1366, partial least squares 0.1376, k-nearest neighbours 0.0708, gene activity 0.0350, depth only 0.0330. The plan reaches 79% of the ceiling.
[P1-E3] (ruler) Margin over the cluster-mean baseline: mean per-gene difference in r = +0.0141 (95% interval +0.0126 to +0.0160, bootstrap over cells); margin over the best simple learner (ridge, PLS, k-NN) -0.0006.
[P1-E4] (self_score) Three-way gene classification by the evaluator's rule, applied inside the development set: 318 genes cannot be judged (ceiling not above the permutation null), 1070 are not beyond the cell-type baseline, 112 are predicted beyond cell type (paired bootstrap against the cluster-mean baseline, FDR 5%; 9.5% of judgeable genes). Genes with r above the permutation null: 1066.
[P1-E5] (convergence) Training: fit 0: closed_form after 0 epochs, converged=True (Closed-form or non-iterative fit; nothing to converge.); fit 1: closed_form after 0 epochs, converged=True (Closed-form or non-iterative fit; nothing to converge.).
[P1-E6] (validation_design) Validation design: split unit cell; 5-fold cross-validation; 3 seed(s); scored against an independent half of each validation cell's reads (unsmoothed, same as the evaluator). Early stopping used a separate split carved from the training cells.
[P1-E7] (validation_design) Scale of this run: pilot; 2 of the 15 declared train/validation splits were run (3000 development cells, 1500 genes; the full problem has 7288 cells and 11282 genes).
[P1-E8] (cost) Cost: 16 s of model fitting on 32 CPU cores (cpu); declared budget for the full run 12.0 min, needs GPU: False.
[P1-E9] (compliance) Compliance checks: inputs_from_view passed; no_label_inputs passed; scoring_target_allowed passed; correct_split_unit passed; no_forbidden_inputs passed; components_executable passed; within_budget passed.

SUMMARY:
We decompose per-gene expression into the nested ATAC cluster mean plus a boosted-tree residual predicted from filtered LSI coordinates and log depth. Inner-fit targets pool eight nearest training neighbours, while per-gene trees weight rare ATAC clusters and early-stop on unsmoothed inner residuals. Three nested 70/30 cell holdouts score predictions against unsmoothed binomial-thinned RNA alongside all required comparators. This tests which genes exhibit predictable chromatin-state variation beyond discrete cell identity at 5% FDR.

[P4-E1] (self_score) Self-reported score: mean per-gene Pearson r = 0.1229 (SD 0.0004 over 2 splits), on 1500 genes; 900 distinct validation cells enter the gene-level tests.

The plan reaches 73% of the ceiling.

Genes with r above the permutation null: 898.

One boosted model per gene on the residual, early stopping on an internal 12% split; 99.8% of 1500 fitted genes stopped before the cap of 150 iterations (median 17 iterations).); fit 1: early_stopping after 17 epochs, converged=True (Base: cluster mean (k 20).
